h1: The 8 Factory Hostel — a vintage hostel with its own cafe and free bikes to borrow
intro: If you're visiting Phitsanulok on a budget but don't want a plain, generic room — The 8 Factory Hostel (Thai name: Hotel Number 8) is the place many travellers remember for its vintage-industrial decor, old objects, classic motorcycles, and an on-site cafe that pours good coffee · It sits in town on Si Thamma Traipidok Road, Tambon Nai Mueang, close to Phitsanulok airport and train station, with both dorm beds and private rooms · What guest reviews agree on: it's clean, the staff are warm, there's free breakfast, free bikes to borrow for exploring the city, and free parking · Mixed dorm beds start around ฿350/night, private rooms from about ฿588.

body.html: The 8 Factory Hostel is a vintage-industrial concept hostel in central Phitsanulok, on Si Thamma Traipidok Road, Tambon Nai Mueang · It opened back in 2016 and was renovated in 2021 · What makes it memorable is the decor — old objects, vintage motorcycles, steel signage and factory-style furniture that give it a character you won't find in your average budget stay in town · It offers both mixed dorms for solo travellers and private rooms for couples or families, around 40 rooms/beds in total.

The rooms draw the most praise for cleanliness · Most genuine guest reviews say the rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, the hot shower runs well, and the linens are fresh · Dorms are bunk beds with cotton duvets, while private rooms like the Superior Twin come with an en-suite bathroom and more space · The basics are all there — hairdryer, luggage storage, towels · The thing to accept is that it's a hostel: dorms share bathrooms and offer less privacy than a hotel — if you want quiet and privacy, go for a private room.
"The room was spotless, the decor is lovely and vintage, the staff smile and are so kind. They give free coffee and fruit, and you can even borrow a bike to ride around town. Great value."

Another star here is the on-site cafe (The 8 Factory Cafe), whose coffee is praised as excellent and which doubles as a nice spot to hang out · There's a small free set breakfast (bread, egg, coffee) in the morning, and many reviews mention the drinks and fruit the owner puts out during the day · There are common areas, a rooftop terrace and a small herb garden to relax in · Frequently mentioned is the free bikes you can borrow to explore the city, which is handy since the main sights are within cycling distance.

Service is another thing that wins guests over · Staff and the owner are praised as friendly, kind and attentive, with taxi booking, luggage storage and free parking on offer · Two limitations come up consistently in reviews — first, noise: some nights you can hear music or traffic from the road late into the night and early morning · second, limited English among staff, so some international travellers keep a translation app handy · If you can live with those two points, the rest is strong value.

The location is in town · Close to Phitsanulok airport and train station, and within a 15–20 minute walk or cycle of the city's main sights · It's not far from Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai), home of the Phra Buddha Chinnarat image, the in-town market, and the Nan riverside night bazaar · The overall score sits around 9.2 from over 120 reviews — high for a hostel — reflecting how happy most guests are with the cleanliness, decor and service.

To be honest, The 8 Factory sells character, cleanliness and value, not luxury or total silence · If you want a full private room, a Nan River view, or the quiet feel of a hotel, this may not be it — look at Dragon River Avenue or Wangchan Riverview, riverside boutiques, instead · But if you're travelling solo or as a couple on a budget, like a place with style and an on-site cafe, want to cycle around town, and aren't too sensitive about night-time noise — this delivers an experience that's hard to find at this price.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you're a light sleeper or worried about noise, ask for a room away from the road and the cafe for a quieter night, and pack some earplugs · For more privacy, choose an en-suite private room over a dorm · And don't forget to borrow a free bike to cycle out to the temples and markets in town — it's cheaper and more fun than hailing a ride.

honestSummary: The 8 Factory Hostel stands out in Phitsanulok for budget travellers who want a stylish, clean stay with an on-site cafe, free bikes to borrow, in town near the airport and train station · The vintage decor, cleanliness and friendly service are genuine strengths — but you have to accept some night-time noise, limited English among staff, and that it's a hostel where dorms offer less privacy.
honestChecks: If you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise — some nights bring music or road noise → ask for a room away from the road and cafe, pack earplugs, or choose a quieter stay if needed
If you want full privacy or are travelling as a family — dorms share bathrooms → choose an en-suite private room, or look at hotels like Holatel or Fortune D in the same city
If you want a Nan River view or a riverside boutique feel — this is an in-town hostel with no water view → try Dragon River Avenue or Wangchan Riverview instead

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The 8 Factory Hostel Phitsanulok

faq.q: Where is The 8 Factory Hostel · is it near the airport and train station?
faq.a: It's at 174/11 Si Thamma Traipidok Rd, Tambon Nai Mueang, Mueang Phitsanulok — in town, near Phitsanulok airport and train station · Both the airport and train station are about a 10-minute drive away · Main sights like Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) and the in-town market are within about a 15-minute cycle — and the hostel has free bikes to borrow.

faq.q: How much does The 8 Factory Hostel cost · what room types are there?
faq.a: A bed in a mixed dorm starts at around ฿350/night · Private rooms like the Superior Twin start from about ฿588, and Family Rooms run about ฿788–988 · It's a hostel with both dorms and private rooms, suiting solo travellers, couples and families alike · Prices vary by date and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is The 8 Factory Hostel best for?
faq.a: It's great for budget travellers who like a stylish, clean stay with an on-site cafe and want to cycle around town · The vintage atmosphere appeals to anyone who loves taking photos · It suits solo travellers or couples stopping in Phitsanulok before heading on to Sukhothai or Khao Kho · If you want total silence or luxury, another hotel may suit you better.

faq.q: Are the rooms at The 8 Factory clean · is there any noise?
faq.a: Most reviews say the rooms are very clean, beds are comfortable and the hot shower runs well, with lovely decor · The point many guests agree on is that some nights bring music or road noise late into the night and early morning — if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the road and cafe and pack some earplugs.

faq.q: Does it have a cafe, bikes and parking?
faq.a: Yes to all · There's an on-site cafe (The 8 Factory Cafe) whose coffee is praised as excellent, plus a small free set breakfast and drinks and fruit during the day · There are free bikes to borrow for exploring the city, and free parking · It also has a rooftop terrace, herb garden, common areas, taxi booking and luggage storage.

faq.q: What are the review scores for The 8 Factory Hostel · should I book ahead?
faq.a: The overall score is around 9.2 from over 120 reviews, high for a hostel, reflecting satisfaction with cleanliness, decor and service · As a popular hostel with a limited number of rooms, it's worth booking ahead over long weekends and holidays, and choosing a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't fixed yet.
